rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes high-temperature tensile, fracture toughness, and nanoindentation creep tests under plasma-facing conditions, whereas the paper used room-temperature compression, temperature-dependent indentation plastometry up to 500 °C, and scratch-based fracture toughness. Both involve mechanical testing, but the specific test types and temperature ranges differ substantially.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis specifies elevated temperatures of ~1000–1600 °C in an inert or plasma environment, while the paper tested from room temperature to 500 °C in air (indentation) and room temperature for compression and scratch. The temperature regimes are entirely different, though both involve mechanical testing at elevated temperature.

rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts higher plastic strain, fracture toughness, and more uniform dislocation activity at high temperature relative to tungsten. The paper found higher strength, greater plastic strain (at 500 °C), lower brittle-to-ductile transition, less scratch damage, and higher fracture toughness at room temperature.
